ReportRequest.description:
POST /reports: the point, the period and the household. The household rides in the body so it is never in a URL
or an access log (D38). Keys are from data_pipeline/config/conditions.json; the service checks them.
ReportRequest.title: ReportRequest

Winters.description:
El Nino and La Nina winters (round 4, D42): how a place's records sat in each phase's winters against the other
winters, detrended, 2001-2025. Describes the past; not a seasonal outlook.
Winters.title: Winters

get.description: The demo cities and their household presets.

schema.title: Response Demos Api V1 Demos Get

get.description: Curated, sourced US events (smoke, heat, cold, rain, drought, fire) for a state or the state of a point.
Trend per NASA grid cell over the lower 48 (built by `python -m tools.trend_field`).

Every grid cell's value for each year on one colour scale, so the map can play through time. Display data:
the trend tests are on /maps/{factor} (built by `python -m tools.map_frames` and `tools.map_frames_na`).

How a place's variables move together (with lead times), signs that its ups and downs are changing, how often
months pass the old top 10%, and compound extremes (hot and dry, hot and smoky). Describes the past; no forecast.
The two records of one link as the test saw them (detrended calendar-month z, 3-month average), for drawing.

Every factor of 51 US cities, for comparing places in the browser: level, then and now, rate, the city's own
Mann-Kendall p and the Benjamini-Hochberg q across all cities (built by `python -m tools.compare_export`).
The place at a spot picked on the map (Photon reverse), or a plain "Picked spot" when it has no name.
Up to 5 US matches from OpenStreetMap Nominatim (1 request per second, stored).

schema.title: Response Search Api V1 Places Search Get

get.description: Up to 6 US suggestions while typing (3+ characters, else an empty list), from Photon.

schema.title: Response Suggest Api V1 Places Suggest Get

get.description: US states (with DC and Puerto Rico), the variables a state can be averaged for, and the allowed periods.
A state's outline, to draw it on a map when someone picks the whole state.

One variable averaged over a state, as a report card with the yearly and seasonal tests. NASA POWER weather
is fetched live the first time (about 1-5 s), then stored.

The trend report for a US point with no household (period is 10, 15, 20 or 25 years, or any start-end of at least
8 years within 2001-2025). Household keys in the address are ignored: send them with POST (D38).

post.description:
The trend report for a US point and household, with the household in the body. Reused from the store when the
household-neutral report exists; the household only orders and flags the cards in the answer.

get.description:
One year at a US point as 52 fixed 7-day weeks from 1 January, each with its usual range (10th-90th percentile)
over the period. A view for heat waves, cold snaps and wet weeks; not a trend test.
